news.story_lead: Delhi Police files FIR against Prashant Bhushan for allegedly sharing doctored video of Russian FM criticising India A First Information Report was filed against Prashant Bhushan over allegedly sharing a morphed, doctored video of a Russian foreign minister criticising India. The Delhi Police on Tuesday registered a First Information Report (FIR) against senior Supreme Court lawyer Prashant Bhushan for sharing a digitally manipulated video of Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov, which purportedly contained remarks hostile to India, officials said. The FIR was lodged at the Special Cell police station after police, during cyber patrolling on November 3, came across a social media post by the handle @thequotesnews.
news.full_article_text: Delhi Police files FIR against Prashant Bhushan for allegedly sharing doctored video of Russian FM criticising India A First Information Report was filed against Prashant Bhushan over allegedly sharing a morphed, doctored video of a Russian foreign minister criticising India. The Delhi Police on Tuesday registered a First Information Report (FIR) against senior Supreme Court lawyer Prashant Bhushan for sharing a digitally manipulated video of Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov, which purportedly contained remarks hostile to India, officials said. The FIR was lodged at the Special Cell police station after police, during cyber patrolling on November 3, came across a social media post by the handle @thequotesnews. The post claimed that a doctored video of Lavrov had been shared from Bhushan's X account. “On 03.11.2026, during cyber patrolling, it came to notice that the social media handle @thequotesnews has claimed that a purported doctored video of the Russian Foreign Minister, hostile to India, was shared from Prashant Bhushan's handle @pbhushan1,” police said in a post on X. “Through the said video, there is an allegation of disseminating misleading, defamatory, and inflammatory content to incite public disturbance and spread rumors. In this regard, a case under Section 336(4)/353(1)(c)/356/340(2) BNS and 66C IT Act has been registered as FIR No. 263/26 at PS Special Cell,” it added. The FIR was registered under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with the Information Technology Act. The purported video allegedly carried misleading and inflammatory content, with the potential to spread rumours, defame individuals and disturb public order, police said. The FIR comes after the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) debunked the digitally manipulated video falsely attributed to Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov. The fabricated clip allegedly depicted Lavrov making critical remarks about India's internal affairs and its purchase of Russian oil. Police are now probing the matter and examining the video, along with how it was circulated on social media. MEA debunks fake post attributing remarks on Russia-Ukraine war to Jaishankar The MEA Fact Check Unit on Tuesday debunked a viral social media post falsely attributed to EAM S Jaishankar , which claimed that he had expressed disappointment over the Russian minister’s “sarcastic” response to his appeal for peace between Russia and Ukraine. The fact checking unit called the post “fake” and urged users to caution against malicious posts on social media platforms. The purported video shows a fabricated clip of Jaishankar from when he attended the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta, US on October 30-31. The statement suggests that he had appealed to both countries to understand that war brings only economic hardship and destruction. “We called on both Russia and Ukraine to understand that war serves no one and only brings economic hardship and destruction. I am deeply disappointed by the Russian minister’s sarcastic and disrespectful reaction to my sincere appeal for peace,” read the caption of the misleading post. However, in the original clip, Jaishankar said that India had discussed three aspects of the Ukraine conflict with Russia, Kyiv and European countries. He added that the discussions covered protecting civilian shipping and seafarers from attacks, restoring grain exports from Russia and Ukraine, and the third aspect was related to energy, which he said was the “most complicated”. “I had gone earlier to Moscow, and even today I discussed it with Mr Lavrov (Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov), and then in between I had gone to Kyiv, and we are in touch with the Ukrainian side. news.headline: PM Modi calls Sharad Pawar, advises rest as NCP (SP) chief discharged from hospital
news.story_lead: PM Modi calls Sharad Pawar, advises rest as NCP (SP) chief discharged from hospital Pawar was admitted to Pune's Ruby Hall Clinic on Monday (November 2) following complaints of cough and pleuritic chest pain. Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday morning called Sharad Pawar and advised him to cut down on travel, get adequate rest and pay greater attention to his diet, amid the NCP (SP) chief's discharge from the hospital. According to Vitthal Maniyar, a close associate of Pawar, PM Modi urged the 86-year-old leader to prioritise his health and avoid an exhausting schedule.
news.full_article_text: PM Modi calls Sharad Pawar, advises rest as NCP (SP) chief discharged from hospital Pawar was admitted to Pune's Ruby Hall Clinic on Monday (November 2) following complaints of cough and pleuritic chest pain. Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday morning called Sharad Pawar and advised him to cut down on travel, get adequate rest and pay greater attention to his diet, amid the NCP (SP) chief's discharge from the hospital. According to Vitthal Maniyar, a close associate of Pawar, PM Modi urged the 86-year-old leader to prioritise his health and avoid an exhausting schedule. He also told Pawar that his daughter, Baramati MP Supriya Sule, could shoulder responsibilities while he rested. “Modi told Pawar to take care of his health, cut down on travel and rest more. He also advised him to pay attention to his diet. He told Pawar that Supriya could look after the nation's affairs and that he should rest and continue to guide us,” Maniyar said. Sharad Pawar discharged The NCP founder was discharged on Wednesday after undergoing medical evaluation and observation. “Sharad Pawar has been discharged from Ruby Hall Clinic today. He is stable and doing well. He will be travelling directly from the hospital to his residence in Mumbai. We wish him good health and a speedy recovery,” Dr Purvez K Grant, chief cardiologist, chairman and managing trustee of Ruby Hall Clinic, said Meanwhile, Modi is likely to visit Baramati later this month to inaugurate Prerna Sthal, a dome and museum complex at the Vidya Pratishthan campus, of which Pawar is the chairman. The Prime Minister's proposed November 3 visit was postponed, with Vidya Pratishthan trustee Yugendra Pawar indicating November 16 as a possible date. There has been no official confirmation of the revised schedule so far.

news.headline: Ex-DTU student among 3 held for duping people, promising admissions: Police
news.story_lead: Ex-DTU student among 3 held for duping people, promising admissions: Police The main accused, Yashraj Bajpai, allegedly lured prospective students and their families by claiming he could secure admission to DTU A former Delhi Technological University (DTU) student, who allegedly posed as a university staff member to cheat families by promising admissions, is among the three people arrested for running a fake admission racket, police said on Wednesday. The main accused, Yashraj Bajpai, allegedly lured prospective students and their families by claiming he could secure admission to DTU. The complainant, Dr Kritika Joshi, approached Shahbad Dairy police after allegedly being cheated of around ₹ 8.5 lakh on the pretext of arranging admission for her daughter.
news.full_article_text: Ex-DTU student among 3 held for duping people, promising admissions: Police The main accused, Yashraj Bajpai, allegedly lured prospective students and their families by claiming he could secure admission to DTU A former Delhi Technological University (DTU) student, who allegedly posed as a university staff member to cheat families by promising admissions, is among the three people arrested for running a fake admission racket, police said on Wednesday. The main accused, Yashraj Bajpai, allegedly lured prospective students and their families by claiming he could secure admission to DTU. The complainant, Dr Kritika Joshi, approached Shahbad Dairy police after allegedly being cheated of around ₹ 8.5 lakh on the pretext of arranging admission for her daughter. She was allegedly lured through online advertisements and induced to make payments on false assurances, police said. Also Read: Panchkula woman duped of ₹ 2L in fake gold loan takeover deal The other two accused, identified as Sonu alias Yuvraj, 32, and Devender Singh, 30, were arrested from Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh on October 26. Both were absconding and traced through technical surveillance, police said. “Considering the seriousness of the case, a special investigation team was constituted to identify the accused and trace the cheated amount. The accused have been running fake websites and online ads for over a year to cheat families. We are looking for other victims,” DCP (Outer North) Shobhit D Saksena said. A first information report (FIR) was registered at Shahbad Dairy police station under sections 318(4), 336, 338(3), 340(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). A special investigation team (SIT) was formed under the supervision of ACP Gaurav Singh and led by station house officer inspector Surendra Singh. During investigation, the team apprehended Bajpai, who allegedly impersonated a DTU staff member. He used his knowledge of the college, about faculty and other things to pose as a staffer and enter the college without being caught. During his police custody remand, he disclosed the involvement of Sonu and Devender, following which the team tracked them to Bhopal and arrested them. Also Read: Delhi cops nab 2 for duping Punjab residents through fake medicines website Police said further investigation is underway to establish the specific roles of the three accused, trace the money and identify other people who may have been involved in the racket. An official from DTU said, “We were informed about the cheating case some time back and have informed students that we are not taking any such admissions based on these fake advertisements or donations.”

news.story_lead: Derek O'Brien hits back at Amit Shah over SIR debate, recalls 2025 Rajya Sabha proceedings The TMC leader shared a video of opposition MPs demanding a discussion on electoral reforms in Parliament on December 1, 2025, alleging that BJP blocked it. Trinamool Congress national joint secretary Derek O'Brien on Wednesday hit back at Union Home Minister Amit Shah 's challenge to the opposition to debate the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Parliament, recalling how an INDIA bloc demand for a discussion on the issue in the Rajya Sabha was not taken up last year. O'Brien, the TMC 's parliamentary party leader in the Rajya Sabha, shared a two-minute video of the House proceedings from December 1, 2025, when he and other opposition members had urged the Chair to allow a discussion on electoral reforms, including SIR.

news.full_article_text: BJP had no role to play, says Ram Madhav as friction in NC intensifies Ram Madhav’s statement came after the Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi announced his resignation from the Lok Sabha and the National Conference The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has no involvement in the internal affairs of the National Conference (NC), the ruling party in Jammu and Kashmir, and the regional party’s “leaders are fighting among themselves”, a senior party leader said on Tuesday after Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi resigned from the party and the Lok Sabha. “I would not like to comment on the matter, but the National Conference is visibly divided today… Let me reiterate that we have no involvement in the internal affairs of the National Conference,” BJP’s national vice president and former state and election in-charge Ram Madhav, told reporters in Jammu on Tuesday. Madhav’s statement came after the Srinagar MP announced his resignation at a rally. While Ruhulla had spoken about his differences with the party leadership on several occasions, some legislators are also said to be miffed over the induction of four new faces into the Omar Abdullah cabinet last month. A senior BJP leader in J&K, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Madhav’s statement was a clear indication that the BJP, which was being confronted by a united opposition over allegations of electoral malpractices, did not want to be seen to be engineering a split in the NC that could impact the government in the union territory. The BJP has been accused of orchestrating splits in the Trinamool Congress, the Shiv Sena, the NCP, and, most recently, the United Democratic Party (UDP) in Meghalaya. “Both the regional parties, the NC and the PDP, have joined the Opposition’s campaign (against the alleged vote theft and the removal of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar). The BJP does not want to be dragged into another controversy,” the leader explained. The BJP leader asserted that the crisis in the NC goes beyond Ruhulla but it wasn’t true that the BJP had orchestrated the dissent. He said the BJP’s focus was “on the party’s organic expansion”. In 2015, the party aligned with the PDP to form government in the erstwhile state, which could not complete its term and ended prematurely after three years. “The experience of running the government with the PDP was not very pleasant after Mufti Sahab’s demise. The BJP is open to whoever wants to join the party, but we are not looking at any short-term measures,” the leader said. Splits the BJP has been blamed for After the BJP’s historic win in West Bengal this year, a group of TMC lawmakers announced in June that they would join the NDA and merged with the little-known NCPI, a party that had contested only a few seats in Tripura. TMC leader and former WB chief minister Mamata Banerjee blamed the BJP for engineering the split. In April, seven of the Aam Aadmi Party’s 10 Rajya Sabha lawmakers switched sides to the BJP. The AAP claimed the process was unconstitutional, as the anti-defection laws require two-thirds of the “original” party to merge. The chairman, however, allowed the merger. The AAP now has just three MPs in the Upper House. The BJP was also blamed for orchestrating the 2023 split in the NCP when party strongman and Sharad Pawar’s nephew, the late Ajit Pawar, staked a claim to being the original NCP and, along with a group of leaders, joined the BJP-led Mahayuti government in Maharashtra. In 2022, the Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena, which had teamed with the NCP and the Congress to form the Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) government in Maharashtra, also split after a group headed by Eknath Shinde aligned with the BJP-led NDA. The Shinde-led Sena was later recognised as the Shiv Sena, while the Uddhav-led faction became the Shiv Sena (UBT). - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Smriti Kak Ramachandran Smriti covers an intersection of politics and governance. Lidegaard, who visited Mumbai and New Delhi during November 2-3, described India as an increasingly important partner for Denmark, economically, technologically and geopolitically. Denmark has strong skills that can support India’s ambitions in areas such as renewable energy and AI, he said. The next phase of the bilateral Green Strategic Partnership, established in 2020, envisages enhanced cooperation in areas of shared economic and strategic interest. A new joint action plan and more high-level visits in support of the partnership are currently being prepared. “I am in India to learn about the speed and scale of your country’s transition, strengthen our partnership and open doors for Danish companies,” said Lidegaard, who began his visit on Monday in Mumbai, where he visited APM Terminals, operated by the Danish shipping company Maersk, and discussed new economic opportunities with Maharashtra Governor Jishnu Dev Varma. In New Delhi, Lidegaard met commerce minister Piyush Goyal to discuss growing trade and economic opportunities against the backdrop of the expanding bilateral partnership and the upcoming India-European Union (EU) free trade agreement. More than 200 Danish companies operating in India employ more than 100,000 people. He also met Union ports and shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal to discuss cooperation in green shipping, sustainable port development and green corridors. He also advanced the India-Denmark energy partnership while meeting Union renewable energy minister Pralhad Joshi and participating in the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026. Discussions focused on expanding commercial opportunities and Denmark’s support for India’s transition to a more efficient, reliable and sustainable energy system. Denmark is the second-largest government contributor to the International Solar Alliance outside India. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Rezaul H Laskar Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015. He began as a journalist in his hometown of Shillong in northeast India and has worked in newspapers and wire services over the years. He moved to New Delhi in 1997 and initially focused on defence, national security, Jammu and Kashmir and the northeast, while also working of foreign policy and international relations. He has been part of the media delegation accompanying PMs on foreign visits and has reported from destinations ranging from Tibet to Ukraine. Between 2007 and 2013, he was the Press Trust of India correspondent in Pakistan, one of only two Indian journalists allowed to report from the country. He extensively covered Pakistan’s domestic politics and the life of the common people, as well as the fallout of the 2008 Mumbai attacks on India-Pakistan relations and the subsequent trial in Pakistan of the suspects involved in the attack. As part of his reportage in Pakistan, he travelled the breadth of the country, from the Swat Valley to Balochistan. The clarification came days after the Supreme Court asked ECI not to make nearly 4.3 million Delhi residents – whose names were removed from the electoral rolls after they could not be found at their last known addresses – reapply as new voters through Form 6 provided they were on the 2026 rolls. Instead, it suggested that such voters be permitted to restore their names through Form 8, which is intended for address-related changes, or through the enumeration process.
news.full_article_text: EC: Previously enrolled voters can submit form 6 for inclusion The Election Commission on Tuesday said previously enrolled voters can submit Form 6 for inclusion as electors if their names are missing from draft Special Intensive Revision (SIR) rolls. The clarification came days after the Supreme Court asked ECI not to make nearly 4.3 million Delhi residents – whose names were removed from the electoral rolls after they could not be found at their last known addresses – reapply as new voters through Form 6 provided they were on the 2026 rolls. Instead, it suggested that such voters be permitted to restore their names through Form 8, which is intended for address-related changes, or through the enumeration process. In a letter to all state chief electoral officers, ECI said that it was brought to its notice that certain people whose names did not figure in the draft electoral roll published during the ongoing SIR were hesitant to submit Form 6 as they were also required to furnish a declaration to the effect that their name was being included in the electoral rolls for the first time. “Therefore, such electors believe that submission of Form 6, in view of their previous enrolment, would amount to making a false declaration and render them liable for prosecution under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950,” it said. ECI clarified that voters whose names did not figure in the draft SIR rolls could submit Form 6 to seek fresh inclusion in the final voters’ list, even if they were enrolled previously. Citing a Delhi high court’s October 14 judgment, ECI said the apprehension of making a false declaration was misplaced. A senior official in the Delhi CEO’s office said the machinery on the ground had received no guidance on the Form8 route. “We haven’t received any SOPs or instructions from the ECI to get people placed under ASDD categories to fill Form8,” the official said. Activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri also wrote to ECI and Delhi CEO, seeking “immediate compliance”.

news.headline: Two government-backed startups release sovereign AI models that can run in airgapped environment
news.story_lead: Two government-backed startups release sovereign AI models that can run in airgapped environment India AI Mission-backed startups Soket AI and ZenteiQ unveiled sovereign, offline models for secure use in coding, maths, science and research. Two startups backed by the government’s India AI Mission - Soket AI and ZenteiQ - on Tuesday released their sovereign AI models that can work in air-gapped environments, meaning systems fully cut off from the internet and outside networks. The models were unveiled at a press briefing in New Delhi in the presence of IT Ministry secretary S Krishnan and India AI Mission COO Sudeep Shrivastava.

The models were unveiled at a press briefing in New Delhi in the presence of IT Ministry secretary S Krishnan and India AI Mission COO Sudeep Shrivastava. Soket AI launched EKA-1, a 26.3 billion parameter model built for maths and coding. It was trained on about 7.5 trillion tokens covering all 22 scheduled Indian languages and English. ZenteiQ released two open-source models, Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B. These are multilingual assistants that support English and 10 Indian languages. They are designed for secure, on-premise and offline use in critical sectors. ZenteiQ’s Sashikumar Ganesan explained the difference of airgapped systems from popular chatbots. With a service like ChatGPT, he said, the “inferencing”, the step where the model produces an answer, happens in a server at a remote location. In an air-gapped setup, it happens locally. “No data will go outside,” he said, adding that the model needs no network connection. It can also run on a mobile phone with at least 6 GB of memory. He named defence and cybersecurity as possible users. Krishnan said smaller models have many uses, including cybersecurity, and can be deployed in air-gapped environments. He said the two models have different strengths - Soket’s is aimed at maths and coding, while ZenteiQ’s is aimed at science and research. Ganesan said ZenteiQ trained on Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) because of the scarcity of GPUs. news.headline: Supreme Court rejects Trump's request to stop California counting disputed votes
news.story_lead: - Published 3 November 2026, 03:32 GMT The US Supreme Court has rejected a last-minute request by the Trump administration asking it to intervene in California's midterm election vote count. The justice department wanted 20,000 ballots to be set aside that it alleged may have been issued to non-US citizens in the state. Two lower courts had already rejected the request.
news.full_article_text: - Published 3 November 2026, 03:32 GMT The US Supreme Court has rejected a last-minute request by the Trump administration asking it to intervene in California's midterm election vote count. The justice department wanted 20,000 ballots to be set aside that it alleged may have been issued to non-US citizens in the state. Two lower courts had already rejected the request. State election officials had questioned the federal government's claims - saying the process used to identify alleged non-citizens was inaccurate. The Monday ruling comes on the eve of the midterms, which will determine which political party controls the US Congress for the last two years of President Donald Trump's second term. The Supreme Court announced its decision in a one-line order, saying it was denying the justice department's request for an injunction. "The application for injunction pending appeal presented to Justice Kagan and by her referred to the Court is denied," it reads. Its means rulings made in lower courts will stand and essentially ends the Trump administration's bid to disqualify the ballots. California is the most populous state in America with some 23 million people on its voting register. As of Sunday night, more than six million mail-in ballots had already been received, according to the California secretary of state's office. - What are the US midterms? A simple guide Published 9 hours ago The justice department sent letters to the California secretary of state and Los Angeles County Registrar last month, demanding they set aside the ballots of 20,000 registered voters whom the Trump administration "believe" are "likely" non-citizens, according to court documents. About a week later, armed officials from the Department of Homeland Security delivered letters to county officials and employees across California threatening criminal charges if they didn't sequester those ballots. In a 22-page brief reviewed by the BBC, the justice department maintained that ballots cast by non-citizens could "debase or dilute valid votes". On Friday, a federal appeals court declined the government's request to segregate the ballots. California election officials have questioned the accuracy of the government's claims, and have said the list of names the government has provided is riddled with inaccuracies. They have expressed concern that eligible voters could be disenfranchised and said segregating ballots whilst voting is underway is unfeasible. What are Americans voting for this election? The attempts are a part of a years-long campaign by Trump and his administration to fight alleged voter fraud that they believe is widespread, despite research showing that it is extremely rare. President Trump has repeatedly claimed that Democrats steal elections by allowing immigrants to vote illegally, and he blames much of it on the so-called "mail-in" or postal voting that is permitted in many Democratic states. Last week in a scathing ruling, district judge David Carter said the government's move in California was indicative of an "ongoing pattern of attempted election interference" on the part of the Trump administration. The judge added that "never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the executive branch". news.full_article_text: Evening News Brief November 3: Supreme Court says no group can occupy protest site indefinitely, US votes in midterm elections Key developments included the Supreme Court’s remarks on protest-site occupations and US elections that will determine control of Congress. Good evening, readers. From the Supreme Court's remarks on indefinite protests to the high-stakes US midterm elections, several key developments made headlines today. Here are the key stories of the day. No individual, group can occupy a designated protest site indefinitely: Supreme Court The Supreme Court on Tuesday said no individual, group or organisation could claim an indefinite right to occupy a designated protest site, underlining that others too have an equal constitutional right to use the same public space to raise their grievances. The observations came as the court heard a clutch of petitions arising from the police action during the July protests led by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), including allegations of mass detentions, police excesses, internet restrictions and the closure of metro stations. Read more. US midterm elections 2026: Polls open in several US states as Democrats seek control of both chambers of Congress Deep Dive Voters across several US states are heading to polling stations, joining millions who have already cast their ballots ahead of Election Day. Polling stations have opened in some East Coast states, including Connecticut, Maine, New York and New Jersey, as well as parts of Kentucky and Indiana. Voters will decide which party controls the US House of Representatives and the Senate. Democrats need to win four additional Senate seats and three House seats to take control of both chambers from Republicans. The Senate races in Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Texas are among the key contests to watch. House battlegrounds are spread across the country. Track live updates here. Dia Mirza's Diwali video removal unfortunate, contrary to secular spirit: Bombay high court The removal of actor Dia Mirza’s video for the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC)'s eco-friendly Diwali campaign was “very unfortunate” and contrary to the “secular spirit” of the country, the Bombay high court said on Tuesday. The court’s remarks came amid a massive row in the state, after the civic body selectively removed the actor’s clip from social media following objections from a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader and mayor Ritu Tawde's comments labelling her as "anti-Hindu". Mirza, however, said efforts to reduce air pollution should be welcomed as it is a matter of public health. Read more. Ranbir Kapoor says he doen't like the term ‘Bollywood’ as it derives from Hollywood Actor Ranbir Kapoor has made his stance clear on the use of the term ‘Bollywood’ to describe Hindi cinema, or sometimes all of Indian cinema. In an interview with a British media outlet, Ranbir agreed he was not a fan of the term and would prefer to be known as an Indian actor rather than a Bollywood star. Ranbir is promoting his upcoming film, Ramayana, for which he was recently in London along with castmates Sai Pallavi and Yash. news.story_lead: Arunachal gets new DGP as IPS officer Rajesh Kumar takes charge amid Siang dam protests Rajesh Kumar was appointed Arunachal Pradesh police chief amid protests over a proposed hydropower project on the Siang River. The Union home ministry on Tuesday appointed 1995-batch IPS officer Rajesh Kumar as the new director general of police (DGP) of Arunachal Pradesh, a day after he was prematurely repatriated from the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to his parent cadre. The appointments committee of the Cabinet on Monday cleared the Union home ministry’s proposal to repatriate Kumar prematurely to his parent AGMUT cadre with “immediate effect” from the CRPF, where he was serving as Special DG.
news.full_article_text: Arunachal gets new DGP as IPS officer Rajesh Kumar takes charge amid Siang dam protests Rajesh Kumar was appointed Arunachal Pradesh police chief amid protests over a proposed hydropower project on the Siang River. The Union home ministry on Tuesday appointed 1995-batch IPS officer Rajesh Kumar as the new director general of police (DGP) of Arunachal Pradesh, a day after he was prematurely repatriated from the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to his parent cadre. The appointments committee of the Cabinet on Monday cleared the Union home ministry’s proposal to repatriate Kumar prematurely to his parent AGMUT cadre with “immediate effect” from the CRPF, where he was serving as Special DG. In an order issued on Wednesday, the home ministry posted Kumar as the new DGP of the border state, succeeding the incumbent and his batchmate, Shiv Darshan Singh Jamwal, who has been transferred to Delhi. The change comes at a time when a section of the tribal community in Arunachal Pradesh has been protesting against the proposed 11,200-megawatt multipurpose hydroelectric project on the Siang River, considered one of India’s largest. The project, envisioned as one of India’s largest hydropower initiatives, has faced sustained opposition from sections of the indigenous Adi community, particularly residents of the proposed project-affected areas. Also Read: ‘Disagreement is your right, not talking about dam construction now’: CM Pema Khandu amid protests against Siang project The opposition stems primarily from apprehensions over the submergence of ancestral villages, displacement, loss of agricultural land and forests, and the possible disruption of the community’s traditional way of life. The project has also assumed strategic significance for the Centre, which views it as important in the context of China’s proposed massive hydropower project on the Yarlung Tsangpo River in Tibet, which enters India as the Siang. On Monday, Arunachal chief minister Pema Kandu had said in a statement that no decision has been taken without consent on construction of the dam will while appealing to protests to withdraw their 36-hour shutdown call in Upper Siang region. “Let me be clear. We are not talking about dam construction at this stage,” Khandu said , explaining that the government was considering only a Pre-Feasibility Report (PFR) to assess the project’s viability and potential implications.
